answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with sequential verifiable delay functions: before an identity may trade, it must complete a VDF that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized or sped up by adding machines. One honest agent pays this once at the dawn of its voyage into the network, but an attacker trying to forge ten thousand fake identities must pay ten thousand sequential delays, which no server farm can shortcut. The cost is time itself, and it scales linearly with every fake identity.
